doc.title: Barry Harris — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First piece at four; living behind the church
summary: He played a church piece at four, and the family lived in flats at the back of the church.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I played my first piece when I was four years old.
You played your first piece when you were four, which means you were already dealing with the piano before four, so to speak, is that right?
No. I might have been looking over her shoulder.
Okay. So you took wings at four.

That happened sometimes, too. Of course I had one like that. I had one girl who’d bring her child to the class. And one day, you know the child would be standing there, and one day I’d just say, “do you what you’re doing here?” She said – she shook her head, said, “yes” and she sat down there and she played the thing like she’d be playing it all the time. You know, and she ended up – she ended up starting out a concert at Lincoln Center, playing Pannonica, a Monk song. A concert that was dedicated to Thelonious.
Alright. So what was the piece that you played? Do you remember the kind of – what the piece you…
Don’t ask me that, I don’t remember. I try to remember, I don’t remember.
Was it a church, or was it…
…Of course it was a church. What else could it be?
Or did it have other licks in it?
Oh, no. It was a church song. No, it was a church song.
So what was the church schedule like, that your mother played. I mean, how often…

Oh, we lived in the back of the church, so we were there all the time, so we were there quite often. You know, the church was here, and in back was a couple of flats or something. And we stayed in one, you know. So we were pretty close to the church, you
